bug_semantics: A crafted DLT_JUNIPER_ETHER pcap processed by tcprewrite can reach the Juniper decoder's embedded Ethernet subdecoder. The subdecoder owns an allocated decoded_extra buffer, but tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state() shallow-copies that pointer into the outer context without transferring or sharing ownership. At tcpedit_close(), both contexts are cleaned: in the reported 4.5.1 stack, dlt_linuxsll2_cleanup() runs once for the outer context and again while dlt_jnpr_ether_cleanup() recursively cleans the subcontext, freeing the same allocation twice and aborting under ASan. This is a local, user-assisted denial-of-service/memory-corruption path through a supplied capture file.
flaw_origin: The ownership error originated in src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_utils.c:tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state() together with the Juniper subdecoder lifecycle in src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_jnpr_ether/jnpr_ether.c: commit 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6 introduced the nested DLT_EN10MB context, recursive cleanup, and the comment 'just need to copy the ptr' followed by ctx->decoded_extra = subctx->decoded_extra. The later linuxsll2 cleanup is the observed free site, not the first root-cause introduction.
ai_marker: none: `git cat-file commit 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6` shows author and committer Aaron Turner <synfinatic@gmail.com>, timestamp 1241816788, and only the two-line message 'add support for subdecoders refs #389' / 'improve JUNIPER_ETHERNET_DLT refs #387'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI attribution, or other trailer.
evidence: Advisory bundle GHSA-7rv6-hjpp-g74c/CVE-2025-51006 identifies CWE-415 in dlt_linuxsll2_cleanup() and a crafted-pcap tcprewrite path. First-party issue https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/926 supplies the 4.5.1 ASan trace: the allocation is made by dlt_en10mb_init(), the first free is dlt_linuxsll2_cleanup(), and the second free is another dlt_linuxsll2_cleanup() reached through dlt_jnpr_ether_cleanup() -> tcpedit_dlt_cleanup(). Maintainer Fred Klassen states there that it was fixed by the #902 work and demonstrates non-crashing 4.5.2 output.

At current src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_utils.c:250-263, tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state() assigns ctx->decoded_extra = subctx->decoded_extra. src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_jnpr_ether/jnpr_ether.c:125-136 creates the DLT_EN10MB subcontext, lines 147-167 recursively clean it, and lines 275-280 decode through it then copy its state. src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_plugins.c:443-473 calls every plugin cleanup and finally frees ctx->decoded_extra; src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_linuxsll2/linuxsll2.c:129-142 also frees that context-wide pointer. `git blame` traces the shallow assignment to 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6 and the linuxsll2 cleanup site to ad31b98a03d34f87155f262fc91799b844dcc38b.

BIC cross-check: `git log --all --reverse -S'ctx->decoded_extra = subctx->decoded_extra' -- src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_utils.c` and `git log --all --reverse -S'tcpedit_dlt_cleanup(config->subctx)' -- src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_jnpr_ether/jnpr_ether.c` both first identify 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6; later hits 77387f1580220c1232a9091c79d0db83ba7ac5b0 and 8df0dbd379053832891fdc1f75485bc223af4e02 are 2013 import/merge aggregates. `git show 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6` shows the single original subdecoder feature commit adding post-init, recursive subcontext cleanup, Ethernet subdecode, shallow state copy, and the helper itself.

Parent absence: `git cat-file commit 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6` names sole parent f41d2a0b319df3e3825007658307e2fb5ce32a2c. `git diff f41d2a0b319df3e3825007658307e2fb5ce32a2c 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6 -- src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_jnpr_ether/jnpr_ether.c src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_utils.c` directly shows that the parent decoded Juniper Ethernet inline and had neither a DLT_EN10MB subcontext nor tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state(), recursive subcontext cleanup, or the aliasing assignment.

Squash/import decomposition: 8df0dbd379053832891fdc1f75485bc223af4e02 is a one-parent 2013 commit titled 'Merged Juniper Encapsulated Ethernet DLT from synfinatic/tcpreplay master - for #42' that re-added 726 lines, while the clone retains the original pre-import history. The vulnerable subdecoder design is already present as the focused 2009 commit 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6, so the 2013 aggregates are rejected as BICs and decomposed to that original commit.

Release boundary: `git tag --contains 8df0dbd379053832891fdc1f75485bc223af4e02 --sort=version:refname` starts at v4.0.0 and continues through v4.5.1; `git ls-tree -r --name-only v4.0.0beta2 -- src/tcpedit/plugins/dlt_jnpr_ether/jnpr_ether.c` is empty while the same command at v4.0.0 returns the plugin path. Thus the imported vulnerable implementation first shipped in stable v4.0.0. The report reproduces on v4.5.1.

Fix boundary and content: direct commit 868db118535a646a8a48c957f1e6367069be1aa7 ('Bug #902 juniper: added safeguards') is second parent of merge 1076f1864237091d0f9abb22499888ee7a9452d9. Its diff parses Juniper extension headers and requires media DLT_EN10MB plus encapsulation 14, returning TCPEDIT_WARN before tcpedit_dlt_decode()/tcpedit_dlt_copy_decoder_state() for the unsupported packet used by the report. First-party PR https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/pull/949 says it protects against invalid or unsupported Juniper packets. `git for-each-ref --contains=868db118535a646a8a48c957f1e6367069be1aa7 refs/tags` first dates v4.5.2-beta1 (2025-07-11), then v4.5.2-beta2 and stable v4.5.2 (2025-08-26); v4.5.1 predates and does not contain it. This is an input-validation mitigation for the reported malformed-capture path rather than a repair of the underlying shared-pointer ownership rule.
reasoning: The crash-site blame would incorrectly select the 2022 linuxsll2 plugin. Following ownership backward shows that the double ownership already existed when 745a71184c9d739305d4319cf2e6bb3998cc27b6 first converted Juniper decoding to a nested Ethernet context, shallow-copied its allocated side-buffer pointer into the outer context, and arranged recursive cleanup. Its direct parent kept decoding state in one context, so it lacked the vulnerable lifecycle. The repository later imported the old work in broad 2013 commits; preserved original history makes the focused 2009 commit the smallest real BIC. The BIC commit object has an ordinary human identity and no AI marker, and its 2009 date also predates modern code-generation assistants, so the evidence supports NOT_AI. The 2025 direct fix rejects the reported unsupported Juniper extension combination before the aliased state is created and entered the v4.5.2 release line, although it hardens the attack path rather than changing pointer ownership.
